items: The Social Good Summit 2026 in Manila will focus on the implications of unregulated AI development on human agency and community well-being.
The event will also feature mini-masterclasses aimed at upskilling participants on data privacy, storytelling with data, and navigating the challenges posed by AI.

MANILA, Philippines – At this year’s Social Good Summit, we’ve chosen speakers who can speak with authority and unique insight about where humanity stands in the artificial intelligence race, and what we can still do to protect human thriving.

In recent months, the threat of unregulated AI development to human agency, security, relationships, democracies, and even cognitive abilities has become an urgent global conversation. That’s why we’ve decided to make Social Good Summit 2026 about this issue, and to spotlight what WE, THE HUMANS can do to protect our communities from the abuses of this technology.
On November 21 (Saturday), at Shangri-La The Fort, Manila, Social Good Summit will convene the following speakers:

items: Three members of the United Nations Independent International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence, the UN’s highest expert advisory body on AI policy-making and governance: UN tech envoy Amandeep Singh Gill, AI Singapore’s Leslie Teo, and Rappler’s own CEO and 2021 Nobel laureate Maria Ressa

Historian, thought leader, and bestselling author of Sapiens and Nexus, Yuval Noah Harari, for a recorded conversation about where he sees AI taking humanity – a unique, longview perspective on how this technology is changing our species

Iza Calzado, a mental health advocate, award-winning actress, and co-founder of She Talks Asia, in a session about how AI, social media, and toxic corners of the internet are affecting young people, families, and communities

Empath founder and CEO Steph Naval, whose company uses technology to improve access to mental health services in the Philippines, on the right balance to strike between automation and the human touch when dealing with mental health, isolation, and loneliness

Senior editors and newsroom managers from across Southeast Asia, on the increasingly critical but endangered role of journalists amid AI-powered disinformation: Wahyu Dyatmika of Tempo, Soe Myint of Mizzima, Mildred Galarpe of SunStar Cebu. They’ll be joined by Kathy Im from the John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation.

blocks.text: More speakers will be announced in the coming days.
RappLearn Mini Masterclasses: Upskilling humans vs abused AI
Aside from the plenary program, there’s more.

A major part are RappLearn mini-masterclasses where participants can get upskilled on safeguarding themselves against data privacy and personal security threats posed by AI agents, vibecoding tools that can free up humans from tasks that can be automated, telling good stories using data, and protecting brands from multiple information crises.

RappLearn is Rappler’s learning and training arm, offering in-demand executive learning sessions in immersive, hands-on formats. At the Summit, we offer modified versions of the full classes, allowing attendees to sample more than one class.
